question: What about investing with Lendingclub or Prosper?

answers: Investing with peer-to-peer lending platforms like LendingClub or Prosper has a fairly high default rate.  I got a much better returns with Lending Club, although in my cases both investments were ok: after 18 months i made 4-5% on prosper and 11-12% on Lending Club. Prosper's rates are really high and why would someone with a "AA" credit need a Prosper loan. Bear in mind that many of the borrowers on these social lending sites have already been passed on by the banks, and the ""credit score"" Prosper assigns to them is absolutely worthless.

history.content: Are all financial advisors compensated in the same way?

Not all financial advisors are compensated in the same way. Some financial advisors are compensated based on transactions, which can create a conflict of interest as they may have a vested interest to churn your account. Others collect an annual fee based on a percentage of your account value, which can be a better option. Some announce that they are fee-based - these advisers often receive fees as well as commissions. Some advisors may also receive commissions for selling certain products, like mutual funds with sales loads or annuities. Therefore, it's important to understand your advisor's compensation structure to ensure their interests align with yours.
How much does a fee only Financial Advisor charge?

You are better served by an advisor who collects an annual fee based on a percentage of your account value. Be suspicious of an advisor with a 1% fee. My advisor charges a monthly fee of $50, but also gets a percentage based portion of certain investments, based on a $150/hr rate that amounts to 4 hrs/yr. Make sure you have a "fee only" advisor who is not connected to a company which sells financial products. Your advisor's compensation structure should be transparent. Check Investopedia for choosing a financial advisor.

Robo-advisers are fairly new. They often don't allow you to pick individual holdings, so these services are best when you want to passively invest. If it supports your 401k plan, you can use FutureAdvisor. The fee is $39/yr, with a free trial. But there are many other robo-advisor start-ups: Betterment, Wealthfront, Personal Capital, Sigfig and Robinhood. Since they haven't been around that long, it's hard to tell how effective these are and whether they beat the market.

No, robo-advisors are not insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC). FDIC insurance only protects certain funds (savings, checking, money market and CDs), and is not meant to protect against losses in the market. A protection similar to FDIC for banks is provided to brokerage accounts' owners by SIPC. Your investment losses are obviously not insured. FDIC and SIPC only provide protection for bank/brokerage failures.
